items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: We were playing down there for Don Roby. He had this place, what's the name of that place, Don? Harlem Grill. Harlem Grill. He was operating this Harlem Grill and we head out playing down there.

ctx.x: John Johnson. You want to go there one time?

Yeah. I want to get that myself up. Well, now, let's see. I was telling you about going down to Houston there. And I learned to lead a bunch of fellas, what the responsibilities was. I did pretty good after that. I got started. And I went off with a, left here, left Sid Isles, and went off with a carnival, carnival show. The boys said they were going down to Mexico, and I'd never been to Mexico, and I wanted to get away and go down to Mexico. So I just forgot about school, went on down there. The old man Sid…

It's alright when the red light go on. Go ahead. When the red light would go on then you start to recording. Now the man in the back that's recording it, there was a little light thread would come off of that disc and it would pile up and then you'd have to wrap it up and take it off and throw it on the floor. And that was one continuous operation until you cut the disc and then the lights would go on and nobody said a word, nothing dropped on the floor, you couldn't breathe too hard. That's right. items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: looked like the same thing happened there that Don C. had trouble with Troy.

ctx.x: I know a question that I play with. Yes that's correct.

I'll play with it. Well then I came out on the house and came on down here and organized a band again in Temple, Texas. I stayed there and while I was there Boots had played with me in Houston and he heard that I was in Temple and Walter Wardell was here organizing the band. Boots told him, I know a way you can get a good first man, a clean tone, nice player. So let's try to get him. Several guys have been trying to get me down here. He brought my hometown, Jack Rampson. He's been trying to get me down here. A…
What year did you join Boots' band when you cut those records? Was that somewhere in the 30s?
